generated.description: The paragraph discussing Krusche et al.'s interactive learning concept spans from page 2 to page 3 and is approximately 12–14 lines long. This exceeds the 10-line upper limit. locations.quote: In their paper Interactive Learning – Increasing Student Participation through Shorter Exercise Cycles, **Krusche et al. have taken up this concept to improve the learning experience in large computer science courses at university [Krusche17]. They introduced an newly developed learning method which shortens the time between theory, which is usually taught in the non-interactive lecture, and practice, which typically follows about a week later, so that less knowledge is lost [Krusche17]. The concept, called Interactive learning, makes it possible for students to transfer the new acquired skills to real, application-based use cases still during lecture [Krusche17]. In order to implement this idea, the lecture is split up into multiple iterations, each consisting of different phases [Krusche17]. First there is a theory phase, before the instructor shows an example to the students. After that the students can try out the concept themselves, before they get a sample solution and instant, but still individual feedback generated by the CI server. Afterwards it is possible to reflect about the newly learned approach. With this fundamental idea, later the assessment management system Artemis was built [Krusche18].**
